papers.title: Letter from the Seathwaite men
lines: Sirs, the graphite has been smuggled again. Three men were seen on the fell with full pockets.
The mine is guarded now. The guard sleeps on a sack of the stuff and says he is just resting.

papers.title: Shepherd's note
lines: Counted forty-one on the fell this morning. Had forty-two on Tuesday.
The missing one is not missing, she is sitting in the gorse sulking.
Gone up with a flask. Back for tea. Probably.

papers.title: Postie's slip
lines: Parcel for Mr Rigg, High Dale. Fell route, four miles, no road, no signal, one bull.
Left under the stone by the gate. The bull has seen me. I have left.

trail.clue: The Post Office stone is a flat slab near the statue. A parcel was left beneath it and never collected.

papers.title: Pressed flower
lines: Pressed between the pages of an old hymnbook, a daffodil, brown as tea.
Pencilled: 'Gathered at Ullswater, April, by a woman who had never read the poem and found it beautiful all the same.'

papers.title: Rushbearing programme
lines: The procession leaves the church at two, carrying the rush crosses.
Then the gingerbread, handed out by the vicar, who gets quite fierce about it.
